title: charts/templates/deployment.yaml: optional pod-scheduling list fields render only when set and default to []
answers: Why does helm lint warn when I set topologySpreadConstraints in values.yaml?
How do I add a new scheduling option like tolerations or topologySpreadConstraints to the MLflow Helm chart?
Where is the pod spec scheduling config (tolerations, affinity, node selector) rendered in the chart?
Why is nothing emitted in the Deployment when I leave topologySpreadConstraints unset?
body:
Path: charts/templates/deployment.yaml is the pod template spec of the MLflow Deployment; chart values for scheduling (nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity, topologySpreadConstraints) pass through its tail, with the topology spread chokepoint at the `with .Values.topologySpreadConstraints` block.
Rule: Emit optional pod-spec fields with `{{- with .Values.<field> }}<key>:` then `{{- toYaml . | nindent 8 }}` then `{{- end }}`, so the key is omitted when unset. Default list-typed Kubernetes fields to `[]` in charts/values.yaml (as `tolerations: []`, `topologySpreadConstraints: []`); keep `{}` only for map-typed fields such as `affinity: {}` and `nodeSelector: {}`.
Symptom: With the default set to `{}` for a list field, setting the value made `helm lint` print `warning: cannot overwrite table with non table` while rendering still succeeded, so the type looked wrong to reviewers.
Constraints: Applies to list-typed pod spec fields; map-typed fields keep `{}`. The example comment for a new field goes above the default in charts/values.yaml, with label selectors matching the chart's own selector labels (app.kubernetes.io/name and app.kubernetes.io/instance).
applies: MLflow Helm chart values and pod template; applies when adding or changing optional pod scheduling fields in charts/.
says: Helm lint produces warnings when configuring topology spread constraints in the deployment chart.
Add support for custom pod scheduling rules like tolerations in the application chart.
Deployment template should omit pod scheduling sections completely when no constraints are specified.
Setting list-based scheduling values triggers a cannot overwrite table warning during linting.
search: In charts/templates/deployment.yaml and charts/values.yaml, optional list-typed pod-scheduling fields must default to [] and render inside conditional with blocks so unset keys are omitted. Map-typed fields like nodeSelector and affinity retain {} defaults, whereas list-typed fields like tolerations and topologySpreadConstraints must not use {} to prevent helm lint from raising non-table overwrite warnings. Example values placed above defaults in charts/values.yaml must use label selectors that match the chart's selector labels app.kubernetes.io/name and app.kubernetes.io/instance.
